Bug_Details:
This assertion will always fail or succeed. If a test subject and the argument to isEqualTo are the same instance (e.g.
assertThat(x).isEqualTo(x)), then the assertion will always pass. Truth
implements isEqualTo using [Objects#equal] , which tests its arguments for
reference equality and returns true without calling equals() if both arguments
are the same instance. To test the implementation of an equals method, use
Guava’s EqualsTester.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by using Objects.equals(x, x), which will always return true because both arguments are the same instance. This is a self-assertion that does not test the implementation of the equals method.
Trigger_Explanation: The test calls the showBug method of the SelfAssertionExample class, which contains the buggy assertion. Since the assertion uses Objects.equals(x, x), it will always pass, but the test is designed to fail because it triggers the bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test run results indicate that the test passed successfully without any assertion failures. Since the SelfAssertion bug involves an assertion that will always pass due to reference equality, the absence of any failure in the test does not confirm that the bug was triggered.
